## Astroinformatics

Interactive companions to the [Astrostatistics lecture series](https://anguswright.github.io/LectureNotes/IntroductionToStatistics_materials.html).
Each page highlights one statistical principle, includes a guided experiment, and links to the relevant HTML lecture notes.

## Browser-native HTML tools

These pages run entirely in the browser without Shiny, WebR, or runtime downloads.

### Priority demonstrations

1. [The Universe You Don't Detect](SelectionEffects/) - selection effects and Malmquist bias.
2. [Noise Creates Massive Galaxies](EddingtonBias/) - Eddington bias.
3. [Many Noisy Stars, One Population](HierarchicalModels/) - hierarchical inference and partial pooling.
4. [Is That Spectral Line Real?](ModelEvidence/) - Bayesian model comparison.
5. [A Sky Full of False Discoveries](MultipleTesting/) - multiple testing.
6. [From Posterior Landscape to Scientific Answer](Marginalisation/) - marginalisation.
7. [Why Reliable Detectors Still Find Impostors](BaseRates/) - base rates.
8. [Knowing the Mean Is Not Predicting the Next Star](PosteriorPredictive/) - posterior prediction.

### Existing inference tools

[Conjugate Priors and the Role of Data](Conjugate/)

[Gibbs Sampling: One Conditional at a Time](Gibbs/)

[Metropolis-Hastings MCMC](MCMC/)

[Shift Fitting under Heteroskedasticity](ShiftFitting/)

### Simulation companion

[Uncertain Encounters, Many Possible Galaxies](ForwardModelling/) - uncertain inputs
in a restricted tidal-encounter model; not a self-consistent N-body calculation.

### Fourier-space companion

[Fourier Transform: Finding Structure in Noise](Fourier/) - reveal coherent
spatial modes in noisy images, superpose patterns, and reconstruct selected
frequencies with a native two-dimensional FFT.

### Further foundations

1. [Correlations That Disappear](Correlation/) - confounding and conditioning.
2. [A Classifier under Alien Skies](SurveyShift/) - domain shift.
3. [Counting Photons](PhotonCounting/) - Poisson arrivals and Gaussian approximations.
4. [Why Stacking Works - and When It Doesn't](CentralLimit/) - the central limit theorem.
5. [Turning Uniform Randomness into a Universe](InverseSampling/) - inversion sampling.
6. [One Bad Star](RobustStatistics/) - robust statistics.
7. [Can You Trust That Bump?](DensityEstimation/) - histograms and KDEs.

All tools are published as native HTML. The original R/Shiny implementations
remain in the repository as numerical references, registered in
[apps.R](https://github.com/AngusWright/Astroinformatics/blob/main/apps.R).
R source and runtime files are not included in the published site.

## Building and deploying

From the repository root, using Node.js 22 or later:

```sh
node deploy.js
node TeachingTools/test_tools.js
HTML_SITE_ROOT=_site node TeachingTools/test_tools.js --browser
```

Chrome is required for browser tests; `CHROME_BIN` can select its executable.
No npm packages or R installation are needed for the build or these tests.

`html-tools.json` defines the published tools, gallery order, lecture links,
and explicit asset manifests. `deploy.js` creates a clean `_site/` containing
only those HTML/CSS/JavaScript assets, shared browser helpers, and the gallery.
Serve `_site/` with any static web server, or open its tool pages directly.
The test runner discovers numerical and browser regressions for every registered
tool, so additions are included in deployment checks automatically.

GitHub Pages must use **Settings > Pages > Source > GitHub Actions**.
The **Deploy HTML teaching tools** workflow builds and tests the actual site
artifact on pull requests and pushes to `main`, and publishes only from `main`.
The historical `docs/` and Quarto outputs are not used by this workflow.
`deploy.R` and `TeachingTools/test_export.R` are compatibility wrappers for the
Node build and export checks, not Shinylive exporters.
